theorem_title: Lemma 2.3 — vanishing expected ambiguity for doubly transitive code families
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open Filter
/-- Lemma 2.3: the field, alphabet size and invariant group may vary with j. -/
theorem erasure_ambiguity
    (F : ℕ → Type) [∀ j, Field (F j)] [∀ j, Fintype (F j)]
    (M : ℕ → ℕ) (C : ∀ j, Submodule (F j) (Fin (M j) → F j))
    (ρ p : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < 1) (hp : 0 ≤ p ∧ p < 1 - ρ)
    (hsym : ∀ j, DoublyTransitiveCode (M j) (C j))
    (hlength : Tendsto M atTop atTop)
    (hrate : Tendsto (fun j => (Module.finrank (F j) (C j) : ℝ) / M j) atTop (nhds ρ)) :
    Tendsto (fun j => erasureExpectation (C j) p / M j) atTop (nhds 0) := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
Let $F_j$ be any sequence of finite fields, let $M_j\to\infty$, and let $C_j\subseteq F_j^{M_j}$ be linear codes invariant under doubly transitive groups of coordinate permutations. Suppose their rates converge to $\rho\in(0,1)$. Fix a valid erasure probability $0\le p<1-\rho$ and erase each coordinate independently. Then
$$\frac{\mathbb E\dim_{F_j}(C_j)_E}{M_j}\longrightarrow0.$$
The fields and their cardinalities may vary arbitrarily with $j$. Ambiguity is the subspace supported on the erased set in the original coordinates.

This supplies the expected-dimension conclusion needed for the auxiliary generalized Reed–Muller code without any extra capacity hypothesis.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: codes over F_{q_j}, independent erasures at a probability p<1−ρ, and o(M_j) → arbitrary finite-field types, an explicit valid probability 0≤p<1−ρ, a finite Bernoulli sum, and convergence of the ratio to zero; reason: finite fields are represented up to isomorphism; probability validity is standing context and M_j is eventually positive
- encoding: invariance under doubly transitive groups → existence of a preserving subgroup with the ordered-pair transitivity property; reason: this spells out both requirements and adds no group or alphabet restriction
